hints: Focus on the word replace. Skin cells are worn away and lost every day, so what sort of long lasting supply system must be in place?
Think about the two jobs a stem cell must do together: make more copies of itself, and also provide new cells that can become specialised.
walkthrough:
**What does the skin need?**

Skin is a tissue with a high cell turnover. Old cells are constantly shed, so new skin cells must be supplied continuously throughout life, not just at birth.

**What is the special stem cell trick?**

Stem cells are undifferentiated, but the key is self renewal. They divide by mitosis so one daughter stays as a stem cell and the other daughter can go on to differentiate.

**Choose the complete explanation**

Differentiation alone is not enough, because the stem cell would be used up. Continuous mitosis plus differentiation gives a permanent replacement system, which matches option C.

options.A: Being undifferentiated and present at birth is true, but it does not explain how new cells are supplied continuously for replacement.
options.B: Differentiation to form skin cells is part of the story, but on its own it would use up the stem cells with no renewal.
options.C: Mitosis allows self renewal to keep the stem cell pool, while also supplying daughter cells that can differentiate into new skin cells.
options.D: Having the full diploid number of chromosomes is true for almost all body cells, so it is not the special feature for replacement.
